label: C
question: Which of the following statements regarding 친자관계 is incorrect? (In the event of a dispute, based on 판례)
A: Even if a 조정 or 재판상 화해 containing a statement confirming that there is no 친생자관계 between the 당사자 is concluded, it has no 효력.
B: Even a 친족 prescribed in Article 777 of the Civil Act is recognized as having standing as a 원고 in an action to confirm the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship only when that person qualifies as an 이해관계인 prescribed in Article 865 of the Civil Act.
C: Where, after co-heirs B and C of the 피상속인 A (female) have already divided or disposed of the inherited 재산, it is clearly revealed by a final and conclusive judgment confirming the existence of a 친생자관계 that D is A’s 자(子), the proviso to Article 860 of the Civil Act concerning the limitation on the 소급효 of 인지 does not apply, and therefore D cannot deny the validity of the 분할 or 처분 made by B and C.
D: Where a child born through 인공수정 is born between a husband and wife who are living a normal 혼인생활, the child born through 인공수정 is presumed to be the 남편의 자녀, and if the husband later retracts his consent to the 인공수정 and files an action to disavow paternity, such action is not 허용된다.
E: A 성별 정정 must not be denied merely on the ground that a transgender person has a minor 자녀, without making a 실질적 determination by considering various 사정 for balancing 법익 so as to harmonize the protection of the transgender person’s 기본권 with the protection and welfare of the minor child.
supporting_precedents: {"[2015MEU0000]": "We examine the grounds for appeal.\\n\\n1. 사건의 개요와 issue\\n가. 사건의 개요\\nNon-party 1(1909. 8. 10. 사망)은 2010. 8. 15. 건국훈장 4등급 애국장 포상대상자로 지정되었다. 그런데 Non-party 1의 장녀 Non-party 2(사망)의 자녀인 Non-party 3이 administrative litigation을 통해 구 독립유공자예우에 관한 법률(2012. 2. 17. 법률 제11332호로 개정되기 전의 것, 이하 'former Independence Merit Treatment Act')에 따른 독립유공자의 유족으로 인정되자, Non-party 1의 장남 Non-party 4(사망)의 손자인 Plaintiff가 Prosecutor를 상대로 Non-party 1과 Non-party 2 사이에 natural parent-child relationship가 존재하지 않는다는 confirmation 등을 구하는 이 사건 소를 제기하였다.\\nThe lower court는, 설령 Plaintiff가 위와 같은 judgment를 받더라도 former Independence Merit Treatment Act 기준에 따른 bereaved family member of a person of distinguished service to independence로 등록될 수 없고, 달리 친생자관계부존재확인을 구할 legal interest도 없다는 이유로 이 사건 소를 dismissed as inadmissible 하였다. 이에 Plaintiff는 자신이 Non-party 1과 Civil Act Article 777의 kinship relationship에 있으므로 prior Supreme Court precedents에 따라 당연히 action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship을 제기할 interest가 있다고 주장하며 appealed 했다.\\n\\nb. Issue in this case\\nThe issue in this case is whether Plaintiff가 단지 Non-party 1과 kinship relationship에 있다는 사실만으로 automatically 친생자관계존부확인의 소를 제기할 수 있는지이다. 이를 판단하기 위해 먼저 Civil Act Article 865에 의한 action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship의 standing as Plaintiff 범위를 보고, 다음으로 Civil Act Article 777의 kin이 그러한 status relationship만으로 당연히 such action을 제기할 수 있다고 본 prior Supreme Court precedents를 maintain할 것인지 검토한다.\\n\\n2. Civil Act Article 865에 의한 standing as Plaintiff\\n가. Persons entitled to file\\n부모와 자녀의 parent-child relationship은 blood-based natural parent-child relationship과 parties' intent에 기초한 adoptive parent-child relationship으로 나뉜다. Natural parent-child relationship에 관해 Civil Act는 모자관계와 달리, father-child relationship의 성립과 해소에 관한 several provisions를 두고 있다. 여기에는 혼인 중 임신한 자녀를 남편의 자녀로 추정하는 presumption of legitimacy Article 844 paragraph (1), 그 번복수단인 disavowal of paternity Articles 846 through 851, 재혼한 여자의 출산에 관한 court determination of paternity Article 845, illegitimate child acknowledgment Articles 855 paragraph (1) and 863, acknowledgment revocation and objection Articles 861 and 862가 포함된다. Therefore, legal natural parent-child relationship의 establishment or dissolution을 구하는 litigation에서는, 원칙적으로 each provision에 expressly specified된 person entitled to file suit가 요건을 갖춘 경우 소를 제기한다.\\nCivil Act Article 865 paragraph (1), hereinafter the 'provision at issue', states that a person who may institute an action pursuant to Article 845, Article 846, Article 848, Article 850, Article 851, Article 862, or Article 863 may institute an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship on another ground. 이는 legal parent-child relationship과 family relations register상의 기재가 일치하지 않을 때 이를 바로잡기 위한 제도이다.\\nThe provision at issue는 who may file such action을 직접 구체적으로 규정하지 않고, similar purpose의 다른 litigation procedures를 reference하며 그 제소권자에게 standing as Plaintiff를 부여하면서 cause만 다르게 하고 있다. 그래서 이 action은 legal natural parent-child relationship의 establishment or dissolution에 관한 other litigation procedures에 대해 supplementary하다. 따라서 the form, wording, structure, 그리고 보충성을 고려하면, such action을 제기할 수 있는 자는 이 사건 조항이 정한 제소권자로 limited된다고 보는 것이 타당하다.\\n\\nb. Specific scope of standing as Plaintiff\\n(1) Father, mother, and child as parties\\nNatural parent-child relationship의 parties인 father, mother, child는 이 사건 조항에 열거된 Civil Act Articles 845, 846, 862, 863에 의해 suit를 제기할 수 있는 자이므로, 다른 사유를 원인으로 하는 경우 such action for confirmation을 제기할 수 있다.\\n\\n(2) Lineal descendants of the child and their legal representatives\\nNatural parent-child relationship의 party인 child의 lineal descendants와 their legal representatives도 Civil Act Article 863에 의해 suit를 제기할 수 있는 자이므로, 다른 사유를 원인으로 하는 경우 such action을 제기할 수 있다.\\n\\n(3) Adult guardians, testamentary executors, and lineal ascendants or descendants of the husband or wife\\nCivil Act Articles 848, 850, 851은 모두 disavowal of paternity의 basic provision인 Article 846을 전제로 standing을 supplementary하게 expand하는 규정이다. 따라서 Article 848, 850, 851의 persons entitled to sue인 adult guardian, testamentary executor, 그리고 spouse의 lineal ascendants or descendants는 those provisions의 requirements를 충족한 경우에만 standing as Plaintiff가 있다. 즉 adult guardian은 husband or wife가 adult guardianship under Article 848을 받게 된 때, testamentary executor는 spouse가 will로 natural parent-child relationship을 deny하는 의사를 표시한 때 Article 850에 따라, 그리고 spouse의 lineal ascendants or descendants는 husband가 child's birth 전에 사망하거나 spouse가 disavowal filing period 내에 사망한 때 Article 851에 따라 비로소 such action을 제기할 수 있다. If not, they do not necessarily have standing as Plaintiff.\\n\\n(4) Interested persons\\nInterested person은 이 사건 조항에 열거된 Article 862에 따라 다른 사유를 원인으로 such action을 제기할 수 있다. 여기서 interested person은 other persons 사이의 natural parent-child relationship의 existence or nonexistence에 대한 final judgment로 인해 certain rights를 얻거나 obligations을 면하는 등 legal interest가 있는 third party를 뜻한다. 따라서 other persons 사이의 natural parent-child relationship의 existence or nonexistence가 judicial determination으로 인해 inheritance, support, or the like에 관한 자신의 rights or obligations or legal status에 concrete effect를 줄 때에만 interested person으로서 such action을 제기할 수 있다.\\nFamily relations register상 친족관계가 드러나지 않더라도 자신이 child's biological father or mother라고 주장하며 such action을 제기한 사람은, judgment result에 따라 the very existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship with the party에 directly affected되므로 interested persons에 포함된다.\\n결국 Plaintiff가 위 (1), (2), (3)처럼 automatically standing이 인정되는 사람이 아니라면, 여기서 말하는 interested persons에 해당하는 경우에만 standing이 있다. Such determination must be made case by case by examining the Plaintiff's allegations and pleadings, and what concrete impact exists on Plaintiff's rights or obligations concerning inheritance, support, or the like, or on legal status.\\n\\n3. Whether kin under Civil Act Article 777 may necessarily file\\n가. Prior Supreme Court precedents\\nSupreme Court en banc Decision 80MEU60, rendered on October 13, 1981, held that Article 35 of the former Act on Personal Status Litigation, which applied mutatis mutandis Article 26 stating that 'the party, the legal representative, or the kin within the meaning of Civil Act Article 777 may file an action for nullity of marriage at any time', also applied to Article 865's action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship, and therefore standing as Plaintiff was necessarily recognized merely by kinship under Civil Act Article 777.\\nThereafter, the Court reached the same conclusion both under the former Act on Personal Status Litigation, e.g. Supreme Court Decisions 81MEU77 and 90MEU347, and under the Family Litigation Act newly enacted after the repeal of that Act, e.g. Supreme Court Decisions 97MEU1585 and 2003MEU2503.\\n\\nb. Necessity of changing precedent\\n그러나 the repeal of the former Act on Personal Status Litigation, the enactment and implementation of the Family Litigation Act, abolition of the head-of-family system, the special nature of status litigation, diversification of family composition and respect for the parties' intent, and balance with other procedures for establishment or dissolution of legal natural parent-child relationship을 고려하면, Civil Act Article 777의 kinship만으로 당연히 such action을 제기할 수 있다고 본 prior precedents는 더 이상 유지될 수 없다.\\n(1) Former Act on Personal Status Litigation에는 Civil Procedure Act에 대한 special provisions로서 Civil Act Article 777의 kin이 necessarily such action을 제기할 수 있다는 express provision Articles 35 and 26이 있었다. But the Family Litigation Act, which integrated the former Act on Personal Status Litigation and the former Family Affairs Adjudication Act, contains no provision at all concerning who may file such action. It only applies mutatis mutandis the provisions on the opposing party in actions for nullity of marriage, etc. Article 24, but not the provisions on the person entitled to sue Article 23. Thus the legal basis of the prior precedents disappeared.\\n(2) 사회와 family system이 변하면서, marriage relation과 함께 family relation의 foundation을 이루는 natural parent-child relationship에 대한 social perception도 변화하였다. The household head system under which family relations were publicly recorded in the family register organized by household unit was abolished in 2005. Then, when the Family Relations Registration Act came into force on 2008. 1. 1., the family relations registration register recorded family relations centered on the individual. Also, nuclear family became the norm and individualism and liberalism spread widely in family life. 따라서 today the legal and social basis for viewing kin under Article 777 as having close status-related legal interest has weakened.\\n(3) Action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship is a procedure to correct family relations registration entries not matching true blood relationship. But today family relations are formed not only on blood ties but also on parties' intent. The Court held that presumption of legitimacy applies even to a child born through artificial insemination during marriage, and even if a child conceived and born during marriage has no blood relationship with the husband, it cannot be said that the presumption does not apply, see 2016MEU2510. The Court also held that if a party registers a child as born of the party's own biological child with the intent to create an adoptive parent-child relationship, adoption effect is recognized if requirements are met, and a claim for confirmation of nonexistence is not permitted, see 2000MEU1493. Thus, while respecting parties' free intent regarding legal parent-child relationship, certain limits are needed so third parties do not improperly intervene.\\n(4) Such action falls under Category A family litigation case under the Family Litigation Act. Its judgment effect extends to third parties, the court investigates facts ex officio and may examine the parties at any time. In particular, because blood relationship can now be proved relatively easily through DNA testing, broadly expanding third parties who may contest existence or nonexistence in the name of truth would likely undermine the stability of status order and infringe autonomous decision-making regarding marriage and family life. So expanding, by interpretation alone and without express statutory basis, the scope of third parties who may bring such action is not desirable. Article 24 paragraph (2) and Article 28 of the Family Litigation Act concerning cases where a third party files such action are provisions on the opposing party, not on the person entitled to sue, so they cannot expand that scope.\\n(5) Since this action is supplementary to other procedures aimed at establishment or dissolution of legal natural parent-child relationship, where it may be filed under another procedure it is not allowed. Also, although in practice it is often used instead of other more stringent procedures, and the Court extended the legal principles to adoptive parent-child relationships, the filing period is otherwise not prescribed except where one or both parties have died. Since the filing requirements have already been relaxed in several respects, further expanding standing to kin under Article 777 is not balanced and may turn this action into a means of evading statutory requirements.\\n(6) Natural parent-child relationship may affect inheritance among relatives and various legal relations such as parental authority and support, so certain third parties should have opportunity to contest it through proper judicial procedure. But the Civil Act already allows a third party who is not a party to contest it if that person qualifies as an interested person. Thus even if not every kin under Article 777 is given standing, the rights or judicial remedy of third parties with legal interest are not unjustly restricted.\\n\\nc. Change in precedent\\nAccordingly, Supreme Court Decision 97MEU1585 and Supreme Court Decision 2003MEU2503, and other judgments to the same effect, are changed to the extent inconsistent with this judgment.\\n\\n4. Determination in this case\\n가. According to the lower court judgment, the following facts can be found.\\n(1) Non-party 1 was designated on 2010. 8. 15. as a recipient candidate for the Patriotic Medal, Grade 4, and his children were eldest son Non-party 4, eldest daughter Non-party 2, and second daughter Non-party 5. Non-party 4, his spouse and children, and Non-party 5 and her spouse all died before the designation date. The only surviving child of Non-party 5 was Non-party 6. Plaintiff is Non-party 4's grandson.\\n(2) On 2010. 8. 30. Non-party 6 applied to the Gwangju Regional Office of Patriots and Veterans Affairs for registration as a bereaved family member under Article 6 of the former Independence Merit Treatment Act on the ground that he is a grandson of Non-party 1, and was registered on 2011. 11. 24. as the first-priority bereaved family member.\\n(3) Non-party 3 applied on 2011. 11. 25. for registration asserting that she is the child of Non-party 1's eldest daughter Non-party 2 and thus first in priority among grandchildren, but the head of the office rejected it on 2011. 11. 30. Thereafter Non-party 3 filed an action for cancellation of the refusal, Gwangju District Court Case No. 2011GUHAP4510, won all claims, and that judgment became final after appeal and further appeal.\\n\\nb. In light of the above and the legal principles, the following conclusion follows.\\n(1) Plaintiff is in kinship relationship with Non-party 1 as a lineal descendant, but does not fall within persons whose standing as Plaintiff is necessarily recognized under the provision at issue.\\n(2) Under former Independence Merit Treatment Act Articles 5 paragraph (1), 12 paragraph (2), paragraph (4) subparagraph 1, compensation is paid only to one first-priority bereaved family member, and the scope of bereaved family members entitled to receive compensation is limited in order of spouse, child, grandchild, and daughter-in-law. Thus Plaintiff, being only a great-grandchild, cannot be registered as bereaved family member, and since Non-party 6 appears alive as another grandchild, Plaintiff cannot be registered even if he obtains a judgment confirming nonexistence between Non-party 1 and Non-party 2. Nor does Plaintiff's registration depend on whether Non-party 2 is the child of Non-party 7, the wife of Non-party 1.\\n(3) Even if judgments confirming nonexistence between Non-party 1 and Non-party 2 and between Non-party 7 and Non-party 2 become final, Plaintiff cannot be said to have a legal interest therein. Accordingly, this action is unlawful because filed by a person lacking standing as Plaintiff.\\n\\nc. The lower court's conclusion is proper under the above legal principles. It did not err as alleged in the grounds of appeal by misunderstanding the law on standing as Plaintiff in such action, failing necessary review, or exceeding the bounds of free evaluation of evidence.\\n\\n5. Conclusion\\nPlaintiff's appeal is dismissed and costs shall be borne by the losing party, so judgment is rendered as stated in the disposition. Except for the separate opinion of Justice Ahn Cheol-sang and Justice Min Yoo-sook, the participating Justices were unanimous, and there are supplementary opinions by Justice Park Jeong-hwa, Justice Kim Seon-su, and Justice Roh Jeong-hee.\\n\\n6. Separate opinion of Justice Ahn Cheol-sang and Justice Min Yoo-sook\\nWe agree with the majority on the change in precedent. However, we differ on the scope of persons entitled to file such action and whether Plaintiff falls within that category.\\n\\na. Our view on the change in precedent\\n(1) The provision at issue states that a person who may institute an action pursuant to Articles 845, 846, 848, 850, 851, 862, or 863 may institute an action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship on another ground. So the person entitled to file such action is limited to those specified there.\\nThe former Act on Personal Status Litigation provided that kin under Civil Act Article 777 may file such action. But because the provision at issue already expressly specified the person entitled to sue, the former Act's separate rule created systemic confusion. When the former Act and former Family Affairs Adjudication Act were repealed and the Family Litigation Act came into force, the overlapping provision was deleted, and the persons entitled to file such action became governed solely by the provision at issue.\\n(2) Supreme Court Decision 97MEU1585 failed to reflect the changes brought by repeal of the former Act and implementation of the Family Litigation Act. However, Supreme Court Decision 2003MEU2503 held that kin under Article 777 may file such action as an 'interested person' under the provision at issue. So the current precedent is not that kin become persons entitled to file such action despite no legal basis, but that they become persons entitled to file it as interested persons under the provision at issue.\\n(3) Although the Civil Act amendment in 1990 reduced the scope of kin, 2003MEU2503, which held that kin under Article 777 necessarily fall within 'interested persons', can still be seen as following the repealed former Act. Thus it should be changed. The target of change should be the holding that kin under Article 777 are included in interested persons merely by status relationship.\\n\\nb. In this case\\nThe question is whether Plaintiff, as Non-party 1's great-grandchild, falls within persons entitled to sue under the provision at issue, namely 'lineal descendants of the husband or wife' or 'interested persons'. We differ from the majority and explain as follows.\\n(1) First, on the majority's need-to-change-precedent reasoning.\\n(a) The majority says that because family relations today are formed not only on blood ties but also on parties' intent, the parties' free intent should be respected even as to legal natural parent-child relationship. But action for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship is a judicial procedure to confirm true blood relationship, and the legal natural parent-child relationship at issue is not something determined by free intent. Under Civil Act Part IV, the chapter on kin is structured around Marriage and Parents and Child, and the latter is divided into Natural Child and Adopted Child. This shows that parents and children relationship may be formed on blood ties and intent, but natural parent-child relationship is based on blood ties. The adoption case cited by the majority concerns adoption, where the relationship is formed by intent. Also, in such action admission and confession are not allowed, and prior mediation does not apply, so the existence or nonexistence cannot be determined by parties' intent.\\n(b) The majority seeks to restrict standing so third parties do not improperly intervene in family relations. We agree private life and domestic peace should be protected. Supreme Court en banc Decision 2016MEU2510 held that, in presumption-of-legitimacy cases, only disavowal of paternity with strict standing and filing period is allowed to prevent indirect intervention by third parties. But this action is fundamentally different. A relationship subject to presumption can be denied only by disavowal judgment, so limiting standing has practical value. By contrast, where presumption does not apply, the nonexistence can also be alleged and proved in other litigation as a preliminary issue, so limiting standing here does not actually prevent intervention. Allowing certain third parties to file such action can instead finally resolve status disputes and ensure accuracy and authenticity of the family relations registration register. In this case, Non-party 3 already won an administrative lawsuit asserting a natural parent-child relationship and the judgment included blood relationship findings, so blocking Plaintiff's suit will not easily preserve family peace.\\n(c) Judicial statistics show that actions for confirmation of the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship account for 75 to 80 percent of parent-child relationship litigation, and first-instance plaintiff win rates exceed 75 percent with appeals around 1 percent. So in practice it has become the principal form of such litigation. Even today, because registrations often do not match actual blood relationship due to legal restrictions or personal circumstances, family relations registration registers cannot be corrected absent a final judgment, and such action must be filed even where there is no substantive dispute. Also, standing is a litigation requirement reviewed ex officio, so overly strict or complex criteria will increase dismissals and cases.\\n(d) The majority worries that broad standing will distort this action into a means of evading legal restrictions. But that is for the family court to scrutinize and distinguish genuine cases from sham ones, not for standing rules to block filing itself.\\n(2) On the majority's limitation regarding lineal ascendants or descendants of the husband or wife.\\n(a) The majority says such persons may file only when the husband died before the child's birth or the spouse died within the filing period for disavowal of paternity. But because this action is entirely different from disavowal of paternity in structure and legal nature, separate conditions like those in disavowal are not appropriate.\\n(b) Disavowal of paternity may be filed only by one spouse, so Article 851 provides for lineal ascendants or descendants if that person died. However, this action expressly contemplates filing by third parties from the outset, so a structure where descendants become supplementary persons entitled to sue when the entitled spouse dies does not fit. For example, the wife A may file such action against B, her registered biological child, without time limit, and if A dies, A's descendants may file. The majority's filing-period logic becomes impossible to apply because between A and B there is no room for presumption of legitimacy, so there is no date when a cause for disavowal was known or a filing period could run.\\n(c) Parties to a natural parent-child relationship are parent and child. The child's lineal descendants may file such action under the provision at issue and Article 863 without further conditions, and the majority does not disagree. If so, it is balanced and natural to interpret that the parent's lineal descendants may likewise file without time limit.\\n(d) Where a parent dies without filing a nonexistence action and only a testamentary executor is appointed, or adult guardianship begins while no such action was filed, the scope of duties under Civil Act provisions will separately determine whether filing is allowed, so those cases differ.\\n(e) The reasons descendants file after the parent did not settle the register during life vary. In many cases both sides accept the first-instance judgment and it becomes final. There are even cases where someone with no blood relationship claims inheritance after the parent's death based on the register and causes litigation among other heirs.\\n(3) On the majority's explanation of 'interested person'.\\n(a) The majority defines interested person as a third party with legal interest such as obtaining rights or being relieved from obligations by a final judgment. This is almost the same as Supreme Court Decisions 4293MINSANG314 and 90MEU88, both under the repealed former Act, so it is not appropriate to keep relying on them.\\n(b) The primary criterion should be whether the current family relations registration register contains a natural parent-child relationship contrary to true blood relationship and thereby injures the person's legal status based on status relationship, and whether there is a legally protectable interest worth correcting. The majority's criterion, whether the person obtains certain rights or is relieved from obligations, is too broad and may include persons with only property interests such as insurance beneficiaries or creditors of heirs.\\n(c) If interested person is determined case by case from allegations and pleadings, the family court's focus may shift from the subject matter, namely the existence or nonexistence of a natural parent-child relationship, to rights, obligations, or legal status. Also, because this issue often involves public-law status, the family court may be forced to interpret administrative statutes like compensation and benefit provisions in special laws such as the former Independence Merit Treatment Act, which is not appropriate for family litigation. In this case, the lower court actually examined the former Independence Merit Treatment Act and Plaintiff's ability to be registered as a bereaved family member before deciding the blood relationship issue, and such administrative-law-centered review should not become the center of this family litigation.\\n\\nc. Conclusion on this case\\n(1) Plaintiff is the great-grandchild and thus a lineal descendant of Non-party 1 and Non-party 7, so he falls under 'lineal descendants of the husband or wife' under the provision at issue and Article 851. Also, whether Plaintiff can be registered as a bereaved family member under the former Independence Merit Treatment Act is not a matter to be strictly examined ex officio, and once it is shown that the result may affect such registration, Plaintiff should be included as an interested person. Therefore the lower court erred by not deciding whether Plaintiff, as a lineal descendant of Non-party 1, falls within persons entitled to sue, and by denying standing solely because he could not be registered under the former Independence Merit Treatment Act.\\n(2) However, the lower court alternatively found insufficient evidence to conclude nonexistence of natural parent-child relationship between Non-party 1 and Non-party 2 and between Non-party 7 and Non-party 2, and instead recognized those relationships as existing based on surrounding circumstances. That lies within the lower court's fact-finding authority and does not appear to exceed free evaluation of evidence. So even if this action were lawful, Plaintiff's claim cannot be granted. And because only Plaintiff appealed, reversing and dismissing the claim would harm Plaintiff, so under the principle prohibiting reformatio in peius the appeal must be dismissed. We therefore state this separate opinion.\\n\\n7. Supplementary opinion of Justice Park Jeong-hwa, Justice Kim Seon-su, and Justice Roh Jeong-hee\\nWe add some reasoning to the majority opinion.\\n\\na. The majority held that among the 'adult guardian, testamentary executor, or lineal ascendants or lineal descendants of the husband or wife' listed in Articles 848, 850, 851, only those who satisfy the filing requirements under those provisions have standing, and if not, standing is not necessarily recognized. This is reasonable.\\n(1) The provision at issue does not directly regulate who the persons entitled to file such action are. It only says that a person who may institute an action pursuant to those provisions may institute such action on another ground. So the natural interpretation is that such person is one who may file suit by satisfying the requirements under each cited provision.\\n(2) The requirements in Articles 848, 850, 851 are all about the person entitled to sue, not the cause of action. Thus those requirements also apply to persons entitled to file such action.\\n(3) Because Articles 848, 850, 851 are supplementary provisions concerning the person entitled to file disavowal of paternity, the interpretive standard must be consistent. So for a testamentary executor under Article 850, only when the spouse expresses by will an intent of denial may the executor file disavowal, and likewise under the provision at issue and Article 850 the executor may file such action only when the spouse has indicated by will an intent to deny the natural parent-child relationship. There is no need to recognize standing where there was no such will.\\n(4) The separate opinion says lineal ascendants or descendants of the husband or wife under Article 851 may file without restriction. But Article 851 does not simply allow them because the spouse died; it limits the filing period to cases where the husband dies before the child's birth or the spouse dies within the disavowal period. This reflects respect for the parties' lifetime intent and stability of status order by exceptionally allowing non-entitled persons to file when the entitled spouse had no chance to do so or died before the period expired. If, as the separate opinion says, such persons may file without restriction under the provision at issue, that would undermine Article 851's purpose. Bloodless parent-child relationships can also be formed by parties' intent and presumption may apply. But if the parent dies and much time passes, it may become hard to objectively determine whether the registered child is one to whom the presumption applies. Then lineal ascendants or descendants, who could not file under Article 851, might challenge the blood relationship against the parties' intent by filing such action. And where a child born through artificial insemination is registered as a biological child despite no presumption, or a child born out of wedlock is registered as biological child with adoptive intent and requirements met, legal protection should not be excluded merely because presumption does not apply. Allowing the parent's lineal ascendants or other descendants after the parent's death to challenge the child on the ground of no blood relationship may infringe personality rights or the right to pursue happiness concerning family formation. So the separate opinion is not appropriate in saying such action may be filed without restriction merely because one is lineal ascendant or descendant of the spouse.\\n(5) The majority's restrictive interpretation is tied to the fact that the provision at issue designates interested persons as persons entitled to file. Even if standing is not automatically recognized, the action may still be filed where the person is an interested person, so interpreting automatic standing narrowly is proper.\\n\\nb. On the standard for interested person\\n(1) Interested person under the provision at issue is a broad concept meaning a third party with legal interest in another person's natural parent-child relationship. The majority limits it to those whose rights, obligations, or legal status concerning inheritance, support, or the like are concretely affected by the final judgment. The separate opinion says the person must have a protectable interest to correct the family relations registration register, based on whether the person suffers detriment in legal status due to a record contrary to true blood relationship. But in practice these standards do not differ much. Even under the majority, the concrete effect on rights, obligations, or legal status is examined, so a third party with only property interest and no status effect will not be included. It is hard to find cases in prior Supreme Court precedents or lower court practice recognizing such a person.\\n(2) The separate opinion warns that individual case-by-case determination shifts the court's focus from the existence or nonexistence of natural parent-child relationship to rights, obligations, or legal status, or burdens the family court with interpreting administrative statutes. But because the provision at issue expressly designates interested persons as persons entitled to file, the court must first determine whether the Plaintiff actually qualifies as such. That review of party capacity helps harmonize the two principles governing parent-child relationships, legal stability and blood truth. The need to reasonably adjust party capacity and set standards before reaching the merits is not unique to family litigation, and today family litigation often raises public-law issues because legal interests around status relations are diverse and complex. So the side effects pointed out by the separate opinion are not essential considerations in determining interested persons.\\n\\nAs stated above, we give this supplementary opinion regarding the majority opinion."}

{"[2016MEU2510]": "The grounds for appeal를 판단한다.

1. Defendant 1에 대한 상고이유 판단

A. 아내가 혼인 중 artificial insemination으로 임신·출산한 자녀의 parent-child relationship

(1) Whether the presumption of paternity provision applies to an artificial insemination child

민법은 parent-child relationship을 natural parent-child relationship과 adoptive relationship으로 나누고, natural parent-child relationship은 birth에 의해 발생하는 관계로 본다. mother-child relationship은 conception과 birth라는 natural fact로 clearly determined되지만, father-child relationship은 별도의 요건이 필요하다. 그래서 Civil Act는 혼인 중 아내가 임신한 자녀를 husband의 child로 presume하는 presumption of paternity provision을 두고 있고 제844조 제1항이 그 근거이다.

이 사건에서 issue는 아내가 혼인 중 husband 아닌 third party의 sperm을 제공받아 artificial insemination으로 임신·출산한 자녀, 즉 artificial insemination child에 대하여 어떤 standard로 parent-child relationship을 인정할 것인가이다. 현행 Civil Act에는 이에 대한 express provision이 없지만, text, structure, legislative purpose, Constitution이 보장하는 marriage and family system을 종합하면, artificial insemination child도 presumption of paternity provision의 적용 대상이 된다고 보는 것이 reasonable하다.

먼저 presumption of paternity provision의 meaning을 보면, 이는 wife가 혼인 중에 임신한 child를 husband의 natural child로 presume하는 것이다. 혈연관계의 direct proof가 쉽지 않기 때문에 Civil Act는 marriage 후 200일 이내 또는 marital relationship 종료 후 300일 이내 출생한 child를 혼인 중 임신한 것으로 presume하고 있다. 이 규정은 scientific verification이 practically difficult하고, legal marital relation에 있는 wife가 husband의 child를 임신할 개연성이 높다는 social background를 전제로 한다.

또한 presumption of paternity provision은 true blood relationship과 일치하지 않는 legal parent-child relationship을 만들 수 있다. 그래서 Civil Act는 이를 뒤집는 방법으로 action for disavowal of paternity를 인정하고 제847조에서 filing period까지 제한한다. 이렇게 standing과 period를 제한하는 구조 아래에서는 presumption of paternity의 effect가 매우 strong하며, filing period가 지나면 later truth와 달라도 번복이 어렵다. 즉 Civil Act는 child’s status를 quick and stable하게 확정하려는 한편, family peace와 child welfare를 지키기 위해 reasonable methods와 reasonable time 안에서만 status relationship을 다툴 수 있게 한다.

헌법 제36조 제1항의 marriage and family life 보장, 개인의 dignity와 equality of the sexes를 고려하면, 혼인 중 출생한 child의 status는 사회 현실과 legislative judgment에 맞게 정해져야 한다. artificial insemination child도 spouse의 normal married life와 family autonomy 속에서 born한 child이므로 다른 children born during marriage와 달리 볼 reason이 없다.

다음으로, text상 presumption of paternity provision은 conception이 어떤 specific process로 이루어졌는지를 기준으로 적용을 제한하지 않는다. 2017년 개정 때도 이 구조는 unchanged였다. 다른 Civil Act provisions도 artificial insemination child를 배제하지 않는다. 따라서 statutory text만 보아도 적용 가능하다.

헌법 제36조 제1항은 혼인과 family life가 개인의 dignity와 equality를 기초로 해야 한다고 한다. artificial insemination child가 출생한 marital relationship과 그로 인해 생기는 family relations도 개인과 family autonomy에 기초한 것이므로, ordinary children born during marriage와 다르게 취급할 수 없다. child welfare 관점에서도, child를 continuously responsible하게 보호·양육하는 parent에게 status를 귀속시키는 것이 beneficial하다. artificial insemination child에 대하여 natural parent-child relationship이 전혀 없다고 보면, child와 양육해 온 married couple 모두에게 큰 shock이고 child에게는 irreparable risk가 된다.

사회적으로도, husband의 consent 아래 third party sperm으로 artificial insemination이 이루어진 경우 spouse들은 child를 jointly responsible한 child로 anticipated했다고 볼 수 있고, 그 consent를 토대로 parent-child relationship이 형성된다고 이해하는 것이 자연스럽다. husband는 wife의 conception and childbirth 과정에 동의함으로써 참여하고, 그 결과 출생한 child는 marriage during marriage의 child로 볼 수 있다. 따라서 artificial insemination child에 대해서도 presumption of paternity provision을 적용하는 것이 타당하다.

(2) Whether disavowal of paternity is permitted as to an artificial insemination child

원칙적으로 presumption of paternity provision이 적용된다면 action for disavowal of paternity도 적용될 수 있다. 다만 husband가 artificial insemination에 consent한 경우에는, 그 consent가 medical procedure에 대한 것이라 하더라도 결과적으로 future child의 parent-child relationship을 인정하는 취지로 볼 수 있으므로, 특별한 사정이 없는 한 later disavowal은 허용되지 않는다고 보는 것이 맞다.

특히 현행법은 artificial insemination consent에 관한 system이 충분히 정비되어 있지 않아 consent form의 작성이나 보존기간이 불명확하고, medical record가 소멸되는 문제도 있다. 생명윤리 및 안전에 관한 법률상 설명과 written consent이 요구되더라도, 그 내용은 procedure 중심이어서 parentage consent가 있었는지 dispute가 생기면 proof가 어렵다. 따라서 consent form이 있느냐 없느냐만으로 parent-child relationship이 달라진다고 볼 수 없다.

또한 husband가 artificial insemination child의 birth registration을 하고, child를 자신의 child로 public representation 하거나 오랜 기간 substantive parent-child relationship을 유지해 왔다면, 이는 consent와 동일하게 평가할 수 있다. 민법 제852조는 child birth 후 natural child로 acknowledge한 자는 thereafter disavowal을 못 하게 하여 status stability를 도모한다. husband가 birth registration이나 오랜 양육으로 child를 acknowledge했다면, 이후 disavowal 주장은 good faith principle에도 반한다.

B. 사실관계

원고와 non-party는 1985. 8. 2. 혼인신고를 마친 부부였고, 원고는 1992년경 무정자증 진단을 받았다. 그 후 non-party는 원고의 consent를 얻어 third party sperm으로 시험관시술을 통한 artificial insemination으로 피고 1을 출산하였다. 원고는 1993. 3. 29. 피고 1의 birth registration을 자신과 non-party의 child로 마쳤고, 이후 약 20년 넘게 피고 1과 동거하며 father 역할을 해 왔다. 녹취록에도 원고가 당시 무정자증을 알고 있었고, 피고 1을 딸처럼 대하며 결혼 때까지 책임지겠다고 한 사정이 드러난다.

C. Defendant 1에 대한 natural parent-child relationship의 존부

위 facts를 legal principles에 비추어 보면, 피고 1은 presumption of paternity provision에 따라 원고의 natural child로 presume된다. 더 나아가 원고는 피고 1을 자신의 child로 acknowledge하였으므로, 원고가 피고 1에 대해 disavowal을 구할 수 없다고 봄이 타당하다. 원고는 diagnosis 후 third party sperm으로 임신·출산하는 데 동의했고, birth registration으로 이를 public representation 했으며, 장기간 보호·양육하면서 substantive parent-child relationship을 형성하였다. 따라서 원고의 action for confirmation of nonexistence of natural parent-child relationship은 unlawful하다.

2. Defendant 2에 대한 상고이유 판단

A. 혈연관계 부존재가 presumption of paternity의 non-application 사유가 되는지 여부

민법 제844조 제1항의 presumption을 rebute하려면 action for disavowal of paternity와 final judgment가 필요하고, action for confirmation of existence or nonexistence of natural parent-child relationship으로 바로 부정할 수는 없다. 더구나 blood relationship이 없다는 것이 밝혀졌더라도, 그것만으로 presumption of paternity가 미치지 않는다고 볼 수는 없다.

그 이유는, text상 presumption of paternity provision은 blood relationship 여부로 적용 범위를 나누지 않고, 혼인 중 출생한 child의 legal status를 birth 시점에 stable하게 하려는 제도이기 때문이다. 혈연관계가 없다는 사정만으로 누구든지 언제든지 다툴 수 있게 되면, child’s legal status와 family peace가 크게 흔들린다. 또한 scientific paternity testing이 발달한 today에도 family relations는 blood ties만으로 구성되지 않고, marriage나 social parent-child relationships 같은 non-blood family relations도 보호되어야 한다.

헌법상 privacy와 family life 보호, 그리고 status relations의 stability를 고려하면, blood relationship 부존재만으로 presumption of paternity의 effect를 배제하는 것은 타당하지 않다. 오히려 presumption of paternity and disavowal system은 child welfare와 legal stability를 위해 존재하며, law는 the child나 biological father에게 disavowal standing을 주지 않으면서도, spouse에게만 strict period를 둔다. 그러므로 blood relationship 부존재는 disavowal의 ground일 수는 있어도, 애초에 presumption이 미치지 않는 premise fact는 아니다.

B. 사실관계

non-party는 extramarital relationship으로 피고 2를 임신하여 출산했고, 원고는 1997. 8. 6. 출생신고를 마쳤다. 원고는 늦어도 2008년경 피고 2가 자신의 친자가 아님을 알고 있었던 것으로 보이지만, 상당 기간 피고 2와 동거하면서 아버지로서 보호·교양해 왔다. 2013년경에는 협의이혼 과정에서 양육비 지급 등을 내용으로 하는 공증 각서도 작성되었다. 피고 2는 오랫동안 혈연관계 부존재를 알지 못하다가, 원고와 non-party의 다툼 중 이를 알게 되었다.

C. Defendant 2에 대한 natural parent-child relationship의 존부

원심은 genotype incompatibility가 있으면 presumption of paternity의 effect가 미치지 않는다고 보아, 피고 2와의 관계에서 adoptive parent-child relationship도 인정된다고 판단했다. 그러나 위 법리에 따르면 피고 2는 여전히 민법 제844조 제1항에 따라 원고의 natural child로 presume되고, 원고가 action for disavowal of paternity를 적법하게 제기하여 승소하지 않은 이상, action for confirmation of nonexistence of natural parent-child relationship은 허용되지 않는다.

다만 원심의 결론은 결과적으로 유지된다. 따라서 원심이 원고의 항소를 배척한 것은 정당하다.

3. 결론

원고의 상고는 이유 없으므로 모두 기각하고 상고비용은 패소자가 부담한다.

4. Separate opinion of Justices Kwon Soon-il, Noh Jeong-hee, and Kim Sang-hwan

이 별개의견은 핵심적으로, artificial insemination child를 남편의 child로 봐야 한다는 결론에는 동의하지만, 그 이유는 legislation의 부재를 메우는 interpretation에 있다는 점을 강조한다. 또한 종래 판례가 인정해 온 외관설, 즉 lack of cohabitation 등 outwardly apparent circumstances에 의한 presumption exception은 여전히 의미가 있다고 본다.

이 의견은 social change, divorce and remarriage의 증가, genetic testing의 발달, 그리고 child welfare를 고려하면, 기존의 strict approach를 그대로 유지하기 어렵다고 본다. 다만 artificial insemination child의 경우, husband의 consent와 family autonomy, 그리고 child welfare를 토대로 presumption of paternity를 적용하는 것이 타당하다고 본다.

5. Justice Min Yoo-sook의 separate opinion and dissent

이 의견은 Defendant 1 부분에서는 결론에 동의하지만, 이유는 다르다고 본다. 특히 third party sperm artificial insemination에 한정해서는 presumption of paternity를 적용할 수 있으나, 모든 artificial insemination에 일률적으로 적용하는 것은 과도하다고 본다. 또 consent가 중요하므로, consent 여부는 증거로 엄격히 인정되어야 하며, 명확하지 않다면 쉽게 presume할 수 없다고 본다.

Defendant 2 부분에서는 종래의 outward appearance theory를 유지·확대해석하여, social parent-child relationship이 없거나 이미 irretrievably broken down된 경우에는 presumption exception을 인정할 수 있다고 본다. 다만 여기서도 단순히 blood relationship이 없다는 것만으로는 부족하고, child welfare, family community의 실질, 당사자들의 태도 등 구체적 사정을 종합해야 한다고 본다.

또한 이 의견은 birth registration에 의한 adoption effect를 둘러싼 기존 판례를 언급하면서, 실제로는 family law와 adoption system의 변화, family court permission 제도, implied ratification 문제 등을 세밀하게 검토해야 한다고 지적한다.

6. Concurring opinion of Justice Kim Jae-hyeong

이 보충의견은, Artificial insemination child에도 presumption of paternity provision을 적용할 수 있다는 점을 설명하면서, 법률 문언은 고정된 것이 아니라 사회·기술 변화에 따라 의미가 확장될 수 있다고 본다. 또한 social parent-child relationship을 기준으로 친자관계를 정하는 것은 법적 근거가 약하다고 보며, 민법은 birth 시점을 기준으로 presumption 여부를 정해야 한다고 본다.

또한 action for disavowal of paternity에서 spouse의 standing과 filing period를 완화한 개정들을 설명하면서, child에게도 일정한 범위에서 action for confirmation of nonexistence of natural parent-child relationship을 허용하는 해석이 가능하다고 본다. 다만 이것은 family peace와 child welfare를 해치지 않는 범위에서만 허용되어야 하고, spouse에게 인정되는 disavowal system과 충돌하지 않도록 엄격한 기간과 요건을 두어야 한다고 본다.

결국 이 보충의견은, child가 direct interested party인 경우에는 헌법상 기본권을 실현할 수 있도록 적절한 legal route를 열어주되, presumption of paternity system 전체의 purpose를 무너뜨려서는 안 된다는 점을 강조한다.

The Court accordingly dismisses the appeal, and the opinions of the participating Justices were unanimous except for the separate and dissenting opinions noted above."}

{"[2018DA1049]": "상고이유를 판단한다.
1. Civil Act 제860조는 its main text에서 “인지 is retroactively effective from the time of the child’s birth.”라고 하면서, its proviso에서 “however, it shall not prejudice rights acquired by a third party.”라고 하여 인지의 소급효를 제한하고 있고, Civil Act 제1014조는 “if a person who became a co-heir by acknowledgment or by a final and conclusive judgment after the opening of succession claims partition of the inherited property, and another co-heir has already partitioned or otherwise disposed of it, such person has the right to claim payment of an amount equivalent to his/her share of the inheritance.”라고 규정하고 있다.
However, between a child born out of wedlock and the birth mother, 법률상의 친자관계는 the child’s birth 자체로 자동 발생하고, the birth mother’s acknowledgment or birth registration을 기다릴 필요가 없으며, 이는 Supreme Court Judgment 67DA1791, rendered October 4, 1967 참조 and it is not the case that such relationship may be recognized only where there is an entry in the family relation register or a court judgment confirming the existence of a biological parent-child relationship, Supreme Court Judgment 92NU3199, rendered July 10, 1992 참조. Therefore, Civil Act Article 860의 proviso concerning the limitation on the retroactive effect of acknowledgment does not apply, nor is it applied by analogy, to a mother-child relationship that does not require acknowledgment, and it cannot be said on the basis of Civil Act Article 1014, which prescribes the right of a person who became a co-heir by acknowledgment or by a final and conclusive judgment after the opening of succession to claim payment of value, that such person may not deny the effect of the division or disposition of inherited property made by the mother’s other co-heir. The same applies even if the mother-child relationship was only later made clear through the finality of a judgment confirming the existence of a biological parent-child relationship, etc., after another co-heir had already partitioned or disposed of the inherited property.
2. a. According to the reasons of the judgment below, the court below determined as follows. Inherited property that was partitioned or disposed of by co-heirs before acknowledgment definitively vests in the co-heir who received the partition or the transferee, pursuant to the limitation on the retroactive effect of acknowledgment prescribed in the proviso to Civil Act Article 860, and this legal principle also applies where a person who was later determined to be an heir by the finality of an action for confirmation of the existence of a parent-child relationship after the opening of succession comes into existence. The judgment that a biological parent-child relationship exists between the Plaintiff (selected party) and the designated parties (hereinafter referred to as “the Plaintiffs, etc.”) and Non-party 1 became final after Defendant 1 disposed of the real property listed in Attached List 1 of the judgment below (hereinafter referred to as “the Real Property”) to Defendant 2 and completed the registration of transfer of ownership. Ultimately, the Plaintiffs, etc. fall under “a person who became a co-heir by the finality of a judgment after the opening of succession” under Civil Act Article 1014, and therefore may exercise only the right to claim payment of value equivalent to the purchase price against Defendant 1, and may not deny the effect of the disposition of the Real Property, whose ownership was definitively vested in Defendant 2.
b. However, the above determination by the court below is difficult to accept as it stands for the following reasons.
1) According to the reasons of the judgment below and the record, the following facts can be ascertained.
a) Non-party 1 married Non-party 2 and gave birth to Defendant 1, and thereafter divorced, while maintaining a de facto marital relationship with Non-party 3 and giving birth to the Plaintiffs, etc.
b) Non-party 1 owned the Real Property and died on January 27, 2015. After Defendant 1 completed the registration of transfer of ownership on the Real Property on the grounds of inheritance on June 8, 2015, Defendant 1 sold the Real Property to Defendant 2 on June 25, 2015 and completed the registration of transfer of ownership around that time.
c) On February 12, 2016, the Plaintiffs, etc. filed an action seeking confirmation that a biological parent-child relationship existed between Non-party 1 and the Plaintiffs, etc., and on July 1, 2016, the judgment granting that claim became final and conclusive.
2) In light of the foregoing legal principle, the facts above indicate that between the Plaintiffs, etc. and their birth mother, Non-party 1, a legal parent-child relationship arose automatically by the birth of the Plaintiffs, etc., and it is not the case that such relationship may be recognized only if there is a court judgment confirming the existence of a biological parent-child relationship.
Therefore, the proviso to Civil Act Article 860 does not apply, nor is it applied by analogy, between the Plaintiffs, etc. and Non-party 1, and it cannot be said on the basis of Civil Act Article 1014 that the Plaintiffs, etc. may not deny the effect of Defendant 1’s disposition of the Real Property. The same applies even if the judgment confirming the existence of a biological parent-child relationship between the Plaintiffs, etc. and Non-party 1 became final and conclusive only after Defendant 1 had already disposed of the Real Property, thereby making the mother-child relationship clear only then.
c. Nevertheless, the court below, on the grounds set forth above, dismissed the Plaintiffs, etc.’s claim seeking cancellation of the registration of transfer of co-ownership shares in the names of the Defendants with respect to the Real Property, thereby committing an error that affected the judgment by misapprehending the legal principles concerning the establishment of the mother-child relationship and the scope of application of the proviso to Civil Act Article 860 and Article 1014.
